note: Every component this tranche renders must have a governing specification in legal-design-specifications.json. This record names the governing specification for each of the 45 implemented components, and records the one component that has none. No specification was authored by this tranche: unlike Tranche 1, which had to author component guidance for guidance components inside custom-pleading tracks, every Georgia component here was already specified. The gate is therefore a check rather than an authoring step.
whyNone: The nine implemented tracks carry no process_guidance component at all, so no guidance specification is needed for any of them. The one component that needs one belongs to ga-jail-k2, and authoring it would be legal design.

governingSpecification.venue: Statewide statute. The court in which the individual was accused or convicted; if the felony charge was dismissed, the superior court in the county where the arrest occurred.
governingSpecification.filingRule: File within four years of the arrest, in the court in which you were accused or convicted, or in the superior court of the county of arrest where the felony charge was dismissed. Confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing.
governingSpecification.noticeRule: Notice to the arresting law enforcement agency and the prosecuting attorney. This is broader than the other § 35-3-37(j) routes.
governingSpecification.serviceRule: Certified mail, e-filing or hand delivery, certified in a certificate of service naming both recipients.
governingSpecification.signatureRule: The petitioner signs. No verification or notarization is required by statute.
governingSpecification.feeRule: No statutory filing fee is identified. Because the relief is a motion or petition in an existing criminal case rather than a new civil action, the leading Georgia pro se practice does not budget one. Unresolved and county-specific; no figure is quoted.
governingSpecification.feeWaiverRule: Unresolved. The pauper's affidavit route under O.C.G.A. § 9-15-2 is designed for civil actions and its application to a filing in a criminal case is unresolved.

governingSpecification.venue: Statewide statute. The court with original jurisdiction over the offences in the county where the clerk of court is located. This is a different venue formula from the misdemeanour-conviction route, which is the convicting court; for a non-conviction there was no conviction, so the § 35-3-37(m) formula governs.

governingSpecification.noticeRule: Notice to the clerk of court and the prosecuting attorney. Registered mail, certified mail or statutory overnight delivery is sufficient notice under § 35-3-37(m)(1). Subsection (m) states no response or objection period.

governingSpecification.venue: Statewide statute. The court that ordered the First Offender sentence, in the existing criminal case.
governingSpecification.filingRule: File as a criminal petition in the existing case with the clerk of the court that handled the underlying case. Confirm the filing method with the clerk before filing.
governingSpecification.noticeRule: Notice of the petition shall be sent to the clerk of court and the prosecuting attorney. Notice is not a request for consent and there is no advance-consent requirement on this route. The statute creates no objection period and no objection-triggered hearing branch.

governingSpecification.signatureRule: The defendant signs the petition and the certificate of service. No verification or notarization is required by statute.
